name: simple-pm
description: A small project-management backend: people, the milestones they work towards, and the tasks in between. Three entities, two references, and rules that actually distinguish an admin from an ordinary member — only an admin may add or remove a person, and a member may edit nobody's profile but their own.

people.description: Someone who can be assigned a task. Administered: only an admin may add or remove one, because a directory anybody can write to is not a directory.

name.description: Their display name. Required, so a paged list may sort by it.

email.description: How to reach them. Unique across the instance, which is why a second person with the same address is a 409 rather than a second row.

user_id.description: The identity this person signs in as, and the field the `update` rule compares with @user.id — which is what makes 'edit your own profile' expressible. A plain uuid rather than a ref to the reserved `users` entity, because a rule compiles to a predicate over THIS entity's columns and cannot join. Deliberately NOT unique: the playground reuses one member identity across runs, and a real deployment would want the constraint.

milestones.description: Something the tasks are working towards. The plan itself is an admin's to set; everyone reads it.

due_on.description: The date it is meant to be reached.

tasks.description: One piece of work, optionally assigned to a person and optionally belonging to a milestone.

title.description: One line describing the work. Required, so a paged list may sort by it.

description.description: The full detail, if there is any.

estimate_hours.description: How long it is expected to take.

assignee_id.description: Who is doing it. `restrict`, so deleting a person who still holds work is refused rather than silently unassigning it.

milestone_id.description: Which milestone it belongs to. `cascade`, because a task outside every milestone of a milestone-shaped plan is orphaned data, not history.
